overallAssessment.verdict: data/regions/gower.ts is a well-structured location data file with hero copy, key facts, seasonal guide, insider tips, top experiences, FAQs, hidden gems, and food listings. However it cites 'Perplexity research' as a primary source — AI-generated content — which violates the site's no-AI-content policy. Specific pricing claims, operational details (bus routes, campsite names), and event listings cannot be considered evidenced until verified against official sources. The core geographic and heritage facts are stable and unlikely to be wrong, but every price figure and several operational claims must be re-verified. Additionally, the OG/social image referenced in the TS data (gower-og.jpg) does not exist on disk — this is a missing asset that would cause a broken social preview at publication.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: HIGH — the TS data file is well-organised with all required sections. Suitable as the canonical source once claims are verified.
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: MEDIUM — geographic, heritage, and AONB designation facts are stable; all pricing and transport details are unverified AI-sourced claims that may be stale (16+ months old)

verified_or_stable.claim: Gower Peninsula was the UK's first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, designated in 1956
verified_or_stable.note: The Gower Peninsula was designated the first AONB in England and Wales on 3 September 1956. Well-documented historical fact.

verified_or_stable.claim: Welsh name: Gŵyr
verified_or_stable.note: The Welsh-language name for the Gower Peninsula is Gŵyr. Well-established.

verified_or_stable.claim: Rhossili Bay — 3 miles of sand, regularly voted UK best
verified_or_stable.note: The '3 miles of sand' description is consistent with all authoritative sources. Rhossili Bay appears consistently in UK best beach rankings (TripAdvisor, Telegraph, Which?). Not a specific dated award claim — safe to publish.

verified_or_stable.claim: Worm's Head — tidal island, accessible 2.5 hours either side of low tide
verified_or_stable.note: The National Trust and NRW consistently state the safe crossing window as 2.5 hours either side of low tide. Standard safety guidance for the site.

verified_or_stable.claim: Dylan Thomas famously got stranded on Worm's Head as a boy
verified_or_stable.note: Thomas describes the incident in his short story 'Who Do You Wish Was With Us?' from Portrait of the Artist as a Young Dog (1940). Well-documented literary biographical fact.

verified_or_stable.claim: Three Cliffs Bay — three dramatic limestone pinnacles, accessible via Penmaen dune walk
verified_or_stable.note: Well-documented feature of the Gower coast. The Penmaen access route and the Pennard Castle alternative are well-established.

verified_or_stable.claim: Arthur's Stone (Maen Ceti) — Neolithic burial chamber on Cefn Bryn
verified_or_stable.note: Arthur's Stone is a genuine Neolithic burial chamber (Maen Ceti in Welsh) on Cefn Bryn common. The '5,000 years old' approximation is within normal range for a Neolithic monument (typically 3500-2500 BCE). The National Trust manages the site.

verified_or_stable.claim: Three medieval castles: Oystermouth, Weobley, Pennard
verified_or_stable.note: All three are genuine medieval castles on the Gower Peninsula, all managed by Cadw.

verified_or_stable.claim: Mumbles is 5 miles from Swansea with Victorian seaside character
verified_or_stable.note: The distance figure and the 'Victorian seaside' description are well-established and geographically accurate.

verified_or_stable.claim: Loughor Estuary salt marshes — important bird habitat, oystercatchers and waders
verified_or_stable.note: The Burry Inlet / Loughor Estuary is a Special Protection Area (SPA) and Ramsar site for wading birds and wildfowl, including oystercatchers, knot, and dunlin.

verified_or_stable.claim: Gower Salt Marsh Lamb — grazes Loughor Estuary; buy from Weobley Castle farm shop
verified_or_stable.note: Gower Salt Marsh Lamb is a real and well-regarded product. Salt marsh grazing on the Gower estuary is documented. Weobley Castle farm shop existence is stable. Current trading status of the farm shop should be confirmed before publication.

verified_or_stable.claim: Culver Hole at Port Eynon — medieval stone structure built into a sea cave
verified_or_stable.note: Culver Hole is a genuine, well-documented mystery structure at Port Eynon. Its function is disputed (columbarium/dovecote, smuggling den, watchtower). The description as a large stone construction filling a sea cave is accurate.

verified_or_stable.claim: Parc le Breos (Parc Cwm) — Neolithic long barrow near Parkmill
verified_or_stable.note: Parc Cwm long cairn is a Neolithic chambered tomb, dated to approximately 3800–3600 BCE (approximately 5,500 years old). Managed by Cadw.

verified_or_stable.claim: Gower coastline is 'part of the 870-mile Wales Coast Path'
verified_or_stable.note: The Wales Coast Path (Llwybr Arfordir Cymru) is officially 870 miles / 1,400 km. The Gower sections form part of the Swansea Bay chapter.

verified_or_stable.claim: Hillend campsite near Llangennith is popular with surfers
verified_or_stable.note: Hillend Campsite near Llangennith is a well-known, established campsite popular with surfers. Verify it is still operating before final copy review.

verified_or_stable.claim: Joe's Ice Cream in Mumbles — longstanding family business
verified_or_stable.note: Joe's Ice Cream (Forte's) is a genuine Mumbles institution. The business has been operating for many decades. The specific '1898' founding date from the TS file is from AI research — verify against Joe's own website.

verified_or_stable.claim: King's Head pub in Llangennith — surfers' pub with local character
verified_or_stable.note: The King's Head at Llangennith is a genuine pub well-known to the surfing community. Verify it is still operating and trading normally.

verified_or_stable.claim: Patrick's with Rooms in Mumbles — fine dining with local seafood
verified_or_stable.note: Patrick's with Rooms is a real restaurant in Mumbles. Verify current trading status before publishing recommendation.

verified_or_stable.claim: Train to Swansea from London — approximately 3 hours
verified_or_stable.note: Great Western Railway services from London Paddington to Swansea are typically 2h50–3h15 depending on the service (some require change at Cardiff). The '3 hours' approximation is reasonable but should note mode and that times vary.

verified_or_stable.note: The Gower Way is a documented walking route. The 35-mile figure and the Rhossili–Penlle'r Castell description are consistent with published descriptions.
